They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. It is in the file `/app/datapaper.pdf`\n  - A recent paper that uses this dataset is \"Brain-wide analysis reveals movement encoding structured across and within brain areas\". It is in the file `/app/methodpaper.pdf`\n  - A white paper about spike sorting and quality control is in the file `/app/ChenLiuEtAl2023_SpikeSortingQC.pdf`\n- Some parts of the paper that describe the experiment and processing have been copied to the file `/app/methods.txt`. \n- **Code**:\n  - `/app/code` contains code from `/app/methodpaper.pdf`.\n- **Data** from the papers are in the directory `/app/data`.\n- **Documentation** on the **NWB** file format is at https://nwb-schema.readthedocs.io. Documentation about `pynwb` is at https://pynwb.readthedocs.io/en/stable/. `pynwb` documentation is also downloaded to `/app/pynwb_docs/`.\n\n## Decoder Task\n\n- Temporally align based on **Go cue onset**. \n- Extract **2.5 s before to 1.5 s after** the go cue for each trial\n- Use **50-ms-width bins** for computing firing rates. \n\n### Decoder Inputs:\n- Time from **tone onset** in seconds (continuous, time-varying)\n- Whether **photostimulation** is on at every time point (discrete, time-varying)\n\n### Decoder Outputs\n- Lick direction **choice** (left, right, no lick, per-trial)\n- **Outcome** (ignore, miss, hit, per-trial)\n- **Early lick** (no, yes, per-trial)\n- **Tongue y-position**, per-session discretization:\n  - 0: < 40th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 1: 40th to 60th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 2: > 60th percentile of y-position over the session\n  - 3: not visible\n\n## Target Data Format\n\n- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `/app/converted_data.pkl`.\n- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\n\n```python\ndata = {\n    'neural': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\n\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\n    ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\n\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'metadata': {\n        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\n        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\n        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\n        'off_start': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        ...\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Format Requirements\n\n- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\n  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\n  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \n  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\n\n- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\n  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. Data structure is correct - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n2. Dimensions are consistent - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n3. Values are sensible - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n4. Decoder can successfully train and predict\n5. Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\n\n### Consistency requirements\n\nYour processing and formatting must **match the reference papers and code** with respect to:\n- Loading of data\n- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\n- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\n- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\n\nTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \n\nWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \n\nDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above, or the task of training a neural decoder.\n\nCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \n\nYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference papers and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `/app/train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \n\n---\n\n## Conversion Workflow\n\n**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. Spike times are converted to per-bin firing rates in Hz. For each good unit, the bin edges for every trial are built as one flat array of absolute times, `np.searchsorted` gives the running spike count at each edge, and differencing adjacent counts gives the spike count per bin. Counts are divided by the bin width to give Hz. No smoothing, normalisation, or baseline subtraction is applied.\n\nii.\n```python\nedges = (go[:, None] + REL_EDGES[None, :]).ravel()\nrates = np.empty((good.size, n_trials, N_BINS), np.float32)\nfor r, u in enumerate(good):\n    s = allst[starts[u]:offs[u]]\n    # running spike total at each edge; differencing gives the count per bin\n    pos = np.searchsorted(s, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n    rates[r] = np.diff(pos, axis=1)\nrates /= BIN                                  # counts -> Hz\n```\n\niii. This also matches the reference code, which calls `sliding_histogram(..., rate=True)` and returns `binSpikes / bin_width`.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Only units with `units/classification == 'good'` are kept. No thresholds are applied to any individual quality metric. This retains 69,453 of 272,227 units (25.5%), a median of 390 per session.\n\nii.\n```python\n# ---- units: QC classifier verdict ----------------------------------\ncls = _text(units['classification'])\ngood = np.flatnonzero(cls == 'good')\nif good.size == 0:\n    return None\n```\n\niii. `classification` is the verdict of the spike-sorting quality-control classifier described in `ChenLiuEtAl2023_SpikeSortingQC.pdf`.\n\n`units/unit_quality` ('good' / 'multi') is deliberately not used: it is an older label that disagrees on 12.2% of the classifier-good units and is far more permissive.\n\nThe one dropped session (`sub-440958_ses-20190216T162508`) has `classification` and `anno_name` set to NaN for all 1,852 units, i.e. it was never quality-controlled. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. There is no resampling or interpolation, and no per-stream offset to correct.\n\n## 2-e. How is the `neural` data temporally binned/resampled?\n\ni. Spike times are binned into 80 non-overlapping 50 ms bins spanning -2.5 s to +1.5 s relative to the go cue. The bin grid is defined once, as 81 edges relative to the go cue, and reused for every trial and session, so every trial has the same 80 timepoints.\n\nii.\n```python\n# trial window relative to the go cue, and bin width, in seconds\nT_START, T_STOP = -2.5, 1.5\nBIN = 0.05\nN_BINS = int(round((T_STOP - T_START) / BIN))             \n\nREL_EDGES = T_START + BIN * np.arange(N_BINS + 1)         \nCENTERS = REL_EDGES[:-1] + BIN / 2                        \n```\n\n```python\nedges = (go[:, None] + REL_EDGES[None, :]).ravel()\n```\n\niii. What variables in the raw data is `input` *time_from_tone_onset* derived from?\n\ni. From `sample_start_times`, the tone onsets of the session, together with the go cue of each trial. coordinate test).\"\"\"\n211\t    if anno in _ANNO_CACHE:\n212\t        return _ANNO_CACHE[anno]\n213\t    a = anno.strip().lower()\n214\t    out = 'OtherCortex'\n215\t    for name, keys in _GROUPS:\n216\t        if any(k.lower() in a for k in keys):\n217\t            out = name\n218\t            break\n219\t    _ANNO_CACHE[anno] = out\n220\t    return out\n221\t\n222\t\n223\tdef assign_brain_regions(anno_names, xyz):\n224\t    \"\"\"\n225\t    Assign each unit to one of BRAIN_REGIONS.\n226\t\n227\t    anno_names : (n_units,) array of CCF annotation strings\n228\t    xyz        : (n_units, 3) CCF coordinates in micrometres (x=ML, y=DV, z=AP)\n229\t    \"\"\"\n230\t    groups = np.array([_coarse_group(a) for a in anno_names], dtype=object)\n231\t    ap_mm = (CCF_AP_BREGMA - np.asarray(xyz[:, 2], dtype=float)) / 1000.0\n232\t    ml_mm = np.abs(np.asarray(xyz[:, 0], dtype=float) - CCF_ML_MIDLINE) / 1000.0\n233\t    is_frontal = groups == '__FRONTAL_MOTOR__'\n234\t    # Coordinates are NaN for a handful of units; treat those as failing the ALM test.\n235\t    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore'):\n236\t        is_alm = is_frontal & (ap_mm > ALM_MIN_AP_MM) & (ml_mm < ALM_MAX_ML_MM)\n237\t    groups[is_alm] = 'ALM'\n238\t    groups[is_frontal & ~is_alm] = 'OtherCortex'\n239\t    return np.array([BRAIN_REGION_IDX[g] for g in groups], dtype=np.int64)\n240\t\n241\t\n242\t# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n243\t#                              helper functions                                #\n244\t# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n245\t\n246\tdef bin_spike_rates(spike_times_list, go_times):\n247\t    \"\"\"\n248\t    Bin spike times into firing rates, aligned to the Go cue.\n249\t\n250\t    Equivalent to VideoAnalysisUtils.preprocessing_DJ_2022Aug.sliding_histogram with\n251\t    bin_width == stride == BIN_SIZE and rate=True, i.e. non-overlapping 50 ms bins\n252\t    covering [-T_PRE, +T_POST] relative to each trial's Go cue.\n253\t\n254\t    spike_times_list : list of n_neurons sorted 1-D arrays of session-clock spike times\n255\t    go_times         : (n_trials,) session-clock Go cue times\n256\t\n257\t    Returns (n_neurons, n_trials, N_BINS) float32 firing rate in Hz.\n258\t    \"\"\"\n259\t    n_trials = len(go_times)\n260\t    edges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()   # (n_trials*81,)\n261\t    out = np.empty((len(spike_times_list), n_trials, N_BINS), dtype=np.float32)\n262\t    for i, st in enumerate(spike_times_list):\n263\t        idx = np.searchsorted(st, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n264\t        out[i] = np.diff(idx, axis=1)\n265\t    out /= np.float32(BIN_SIZE)\n266\t    return out\n267\t\n268\t\n269\tdef bin_visible_mean(times, values, visible, go_times):\n270\t    \"\"\"\n271\t    Average `values` over the frames inside each 50 ms bin that are marked `visible`.\n272\t\n273\t    times   : (n_frames,) sorted session-clock frame times\n274\t    values  : (n_frames,) values to average (tongue y)\n275\t    visible : (n_frames,) bool\n276\t    Returns (mean_value, n_visible) each (n_trials, N_BINS); mean is NaN where n_visible==0.\n277\t    \"\"\"\n278\t    n_trials = len(go_times)\n279\t    tv = times[visible]\n280\t    yv = values[visible]\n281\t    edges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()\n282\t    idx = np.searchsorted(tv, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n283\t    csum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(yv.astype(np.float64))])\n284\t    counts = np.diff(idx, axis=1)\n285\t    sums = np.diff(csum[idx], axis=1)\n286\t    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):\n287\t        mean = np.where(counts > 0, sums / np.maximum(counts, 1), np.nan)\n288\t    return mean, counts\n289\t\n290\t\n291\tdef discretise_tongue(mean_y, counts):\n292\t    \"\"\"\n293\t    Per-session discretisation of the tongue y position.\n294\t      0 : y  < 40th percentile of the session's visible y values\n295\t      1 : 40th <= y <= 60th percentile\n296\t      2 : y  > 60th percentile\n297\t      3 : tongue not visible in this bin\n298\t    \"\"\"\n299\t    vis = counts > 0\n300\t    out = np.full(mean_y.shape, 3, dtype=np.int64)\n301\t    if not np.any(vis):\n302\t        return out, (np.nan, np.nan)\n303\t    p40, p60 = np.percentile(mean_y[vis], [TONGUE_PCT_LOW, TONGUE_PCT_HIGH])\n304\t    y = mean_y[vis]\n305\t    cls = np.where(y < p40, 0, np.where(y > p60, 2, 1))\n306\t    out[vis] = cls\n307\t    return out, (float(p40), float(p60))\n308\t\n309\t\n310\tdef _read_ragged(col, index):\n311\t    \"\"\"Read one row of a pynwb ragged (VectorIndex-backed) column.\"\"\"\n312\t    return np.asarray(col[index])\n313\t\n314\t\n315\t# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n316\t#                            per-session conversion   'Hippocampal formation', 'Hippocampal region', 'Induseum griseum', 'Fasciola cinerea',\n    'Retrohippocampal region', 'Ammon',\n]\n_OLFACTORY = [\n    'Anterior olfactory nucleus', 'Piriform area', 'Piriform-amygdalar area', 'Postpiriform transition area', 'Olfactory bulb',\n]\n_CORTICAL_SUBPLATE = [\n    'Claustrum', 'Endopiriform nucleus', 'Lateral amygdalar nucleus',\n    'Basolateral is ALM (coordinate test below).\n_FRONTAL_MOTOR = ['Secondary motor area', 'Primary motor area', 'Frontal pole']\n\n_GROUPS = [\n    ('Cerebellum', _CEREBELLUM), ('Medulla', _MEDULLA), ('Pons', _PONS),\n    ('Midbrain', _MIDBRAIN), ('Thalamus', _THALAMUS), ('Hypothalamus', _HYPOTHALAMUS),\n    ('Striatum', _STRIATUM), ('Pallidum', _PALLIDUM), ('Hippocampus', _HIPPOCAMPUS),\n    ('Olfactory', _OLFACTORY), ('CorticalSubplate', _CORTICAL_SUBPLATE),\n    ('Orbital', _ORBITAL), ('__FRONTAL_MOTOR__', _FRONTAL_MOTOR),\n]\n\n_ANNO_CACHE = {}\n\n\ndef _coarse_group(anno):\n    \"\"\"Coarse group for one CCF annotation string (before the ALM coordinate test).\"\"\"\n    if anno in _ANNO_CACHE:\n        return _ANNO_CACHE[anno]\n    a = anno.strip().lower()\n    out = 'OtherCortex'\n    for name, keys in _GROUPS:\n        if any(k.lower() in a for k in keys):\n            out = name\n            break\n    _ANNO_CACHE[anno] = out\n    return out\n\n\ndef assign_brain_regions(anno_names, xyz):\n    \"\"\"\n    Assign each unit to one of BRAIN_REGIONS.\n\n    anno_names : (n_units,) array of CCF annotation strings\n    xyz        : (n_units, 3) CCF coordinates in micrometres (x=ML, y=DV, z=AP)\n    \"\"\"\n    groups = np.array([_coarse_group(a) for a in anno_names], dtype=object)\n    ap_mm = (CCF_AP_BREGMA - np.asarray(xyz[:, 2], dtype=float)) / 1000.0\n    ml_mm = np.abs(np.asarray(xyz[:, 0], dtype=float) - CCF_ML_MIDLINE) / 1000.0\n    is_frontal = groups == '__FRONTAL_MOTOR__'\n    # Coordinates are NaN for a handful of units; treat those as failing the ALM test.\n    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore'):\n        is_alm = is_frontal & (ap_mm > ALM_MIN_AP_MM) & (ml_mm < ALM_MAX_ML_MM)\n    groups[is_alm] = 'ALM'\n    groups[is_frontal & ~is_alm] = 'OtherCortex'\n    return np.array([BRAIN_REGION_IDX[g] for g in groups], dtype=np.int64)\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n#                              helper functions                                #\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\ndef bin_spike_rates(spike_times_list, go_times):\n    \"\"\"\n    Bin spike times into firing rates, aligned to the Go cue.\n\n    Equivalent to VideoAnalysisUtils.preprocessing_DJ_2022Aug.sliding_histogram with\n    bin_width == stride == BIN_SIZE and rate=True, i.e. non-overlapping 50 ms bins\n    covering [-T_PRE, +T_POST] relative to each trial's Go cue.\n\n    spike_times_list : list of n_neurons sorted 1-D arrays of session-clock spike times\n    go_times         : (n_trials,) session-clock Go cue times\n\n    Returns (n_neurons, n_trials, N_BINS) float32 firing rate in Hz.\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(go_times)\n    edges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()   # (n_trials*81,)\n    out = np.empty((len(spike_times_list), n_trials, N_BINS), dtype=np.float32)\n    for i, st in enumerate(spike_times_list):\n        idx = np.searchsorted(st, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n        out[i] = np.diff(idx, axis=1)\n    out /= np.float32(BIN_SIZE)\n    return out\n\n\ndef bin_visible_mean(times, values, visible, go_times):\n    \"\"\"\n    Average `values` over the frames inside each 50 ms bin that are marked `visible`.\n\n    times   : (n_frames,) sorted session-clock frame times\n    values  : (n_frames,) values to average (tongue y)\n    visible : (n_frames,) bool\n    Returns (mean_value, n_visible) each (n_trials, N_BINS); mean is NaN where n_visible==0.\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(go_times)\n    tv = times[visible]\n    yv = values[visible]\n    edges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()\n    idx = np.searchsorted(tv, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n    csum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(yv.astype(np.float64))])\n    counts = np.diff(idx, axis=1)\n    sums = np.diff(csum[idx], axis=1)\n    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):\n        mean = np.where(counts > 0, sums / np.maximum(counts, 1), np.nan)\n    return mean, counts\n\n\ndef discretise_tongue(mean_y, counts):\n    \"\"\"\n    Per-session discretisation of the tongue y position.\n      0 : y  < 40th percentile of the session's visible y values\n      1 : 40th <= y <= 60th percentile\n      2 : y  > 60th percentile\n      3 : tongue not visible in this bin\n    \"\"\"\n    vis = counts > 0\n    out = np.full(mean_y.shape, 3, dtype=np.int64)\n    if not np.any(vis):\n        return out, (np.nan, np.nan)\n    p40, p60 = np.percentile(mean_y[vis], [TONGUE_PCT_LOW, TONGUE_PCT_HIGH])\n    y = mean_y[vis]\n    cls = np.where(y < p40, 0, np.where(y > p60, 2, 1))\n    out[vis] = cls\n    return out, (float(p40), float(p60))\n\n\ndef _read_ragged(col, index):\n    \"\"\"Read one row of a pynwb ragged (VectorIndex-backed) column.\"\"\"\n    return np.asarray(col[index])\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n#                            per-session conversion                            #\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\ndef process_session(path, show_processing=False, plot_dir=\"/app\"):\n    \"\"\"Convert one NWB session. Returns a dict, or None if the session is unusable.\"\"\"\n    from pynwb import NWBHDF5IO\n\n    t_start = time.time()\n    timing = OrderedDict()\n\n    with NWBHDF5IO(path, 'r', load_namespaces=True) as io:\n        nwb = io.read()\n        session_id = nwb.identifier\n        subject = nwb.subject.description or nwb.subject.subject_id\n\n        units = nwb.units\n        if units is None or len(units) == 0:\n            return {'session_id': session_id, 'skipped': 'no units'}\n        classification = np.asarray(units['classification'][:])\n        good = np.where(classification == 'good')[0]\n        if len(good) == 0:\n            return {'session_id': session_id, 'skipped': 'no good units'}\n\n        # ---- trials -------------------------------------------------------- #\n        trials = nwb.trials.to_dataframe()\n        n_trials_all = len(trials)\n\n        # Ephys coverage.  units.obs_intervals lists, for each unit, the intervals the\n        # unit was observed in; every row matches exactly one trial's\n        # (start_time, stop_time) and all good units of a session share the same list\n        # (verified over all 173 sessions).  In 9 sessions it covers only part of the\n        # behavioural trials -- usually a prefix, but in SC026_20190807_134913_s20 a\n        # block starting at trial 126 -- so match by time rather than assuming a prefix.\n        obs = np.asarray(units['obs_intervals'][int(good[0])], dtype=np.float64)\n\n        be = nwb.acquisition['BehavioralEvents']\n        go_all = np.asarray(be['go_start_times'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\n        assert len(go_all) == n_trials_all, \\\n            f\"{session_id}: {len(go_all)} go cues for {n_trials_all} trials\"\n\n        start_all = trials['start_time'].values.astype(np.float64)\n        stop_all = trials['stop_time'].values.astype(np.float64)\n        outcome_all = np.asarray(trials['outcome'].values, dtype=object).astype(str)\n        instr_all = np.asarray(trials['trial_instruction'].values, dtype=object).astype(str)\n        early_all = np.asarray(trials['early_lick'].values, dtype=object).astype(str)\n        auto_all = np.asarray(trials['auto_water'].values).astype(int)\n        free_all = np.asarray(trials['free_water'].values).astype(int)\n\n        # ---- trial curation ------------------------------------------------- #\n        ephys_covered = np.zeros(n_trials_all, dtype=bool)\n        j = np.clip(np.searchsorted(start_all, obs[:, 0] + 1e-6) - 1, 0, n_trials_all - 1)\n        matched = np.isclose(start_all[j], obs[:, 0]) & np.isclose(stop_all[j], obs[:, 1])\n        ephys_covered[j[matched]] = True\n        n_ephys = int(ephys_covered.sum())\n\n        keep = ephys_covered.copy()                 # ephys coverage\n        keep &= (auto_all == 0) & (free_all == 0)   # no auto / free water (reference)\n        trial_idx = np.where(keep)[0]\n        n_trials = len(trial_idx)\n        if n_trials < 2:\n            return {'session_id': session_id, 'skipped': f'only {n_trials} usable trials'}\n\n        go = go_all[trial_idx]\n        timing['trials'] = time.time() - t_start\n\n        # ---- neural --------------------------------------------------------- #\n        t0 = time.time()\n        spike_lists = []\n        for i in good:\n            st = np.asarray(units['spike_times'][int(i)], dtype=np.float64)\n            if st.size > 1 and not np.all(np.diff(st) >= 0):\n                st = np.sort(st)\n timing['bin_spikes'] = time.time() - t0\n        del spike_lists\n\n        # A trial in which the entire simultaneously-recorded population fires zero\n        # spikes carries no neural data at all: it happens when the recording stops\n        # part-way through the session (typically the single last ephys trial).\n        has_spikes = rates.sum(axis=(0, 2)) > 0\n        n_empty = int(np.sum(~has_spikes))\n        if n_empty:\n            rates = rates[:, has_spikes, :]\n            trial_idx = trial_idx[has_spikes]\n            go = go_all[trial_idx]\n            n_trials = len(trial_idx)\n            if n_trials < 2:\n                return {'session_id': session_id,\n                        'skipped': f'only {n_trials} trials with spikes'}\n\n        # ---- brain      # ---- input 2: photostimulation on/off --------------------------------- #\n        ps_start = np.asarray(be['photostim_start_times'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\n        ps_stop =       ])\n            for t in range(n_trials)\n        ]\n        timing['assemble'] = time.time() - t0\n\n        info = {\n            'session_id': session_id,\n            'subject': subject,\n            'subject_id': nwb.subject.subject_id,\n            'session_start_time': str(nwb.session_start_time),\n            'n_trials_all': int(n_trials_all),\n            'n_trials_ephys': 'n_neurons': int(len(good)),\n            'n_units_total': int(len(units)),\n            'n_probes': int(len(nwb.electrode_groups)),\n            'tongue_pct40': pcts[0],\n            'tongue_pct60': show_processing:\n            _plot_processing(plot_dir, session_id, go, trial_idx, rates, time_from_tone,\n                             photostim, choice, outcome_code, early_code, tongue_class,\n 'output': output_trials,\n            'brain_region_idx': region_idx,\n            'info': info,\n        }\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n#                            processing-step plots                             #\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\ndef _plot_processing(plot_dir, session_id, Neurons *are* quality-filtered: the pipeline only ever\n55\t  loads units on the classifier-derived \"good unit\" list (`methods.txt`: 15 quality metrics → 5\n56\t  region-specific logistic-regression classifiers → 'good' labels; 69,943 good units = 25.9 % of KS2 clusters).\n57\t- Alignment throughout the reference pipeline is to the **Go cue**, which is exactly what this task asks for.\n58\t- Firing rates (spikes/s), not raw counts, are the reference representation.\n59\t- The method paper additionally drops neurons with mean firing rate < 2 Hz, but only for the\n60\t  ridge-regression \"predict firing rate from video\" analyses (\"Neurons with low firing rates (below 2 Hz)\n61\t  were excluded from analyses; the results were not sensitive to the exact value of this threshold\").\n62\t  That is an analysis-specific convenience threshold, not a data-quality criterion — see Step 5 decision D4.\n63\t\n64\t---\n65\t\n66\t## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n67\t**Status**: COMPLETE\n68\t\n69\t### Data Structure\n70\t- `/app/data/sub-<subject_id>/sub-<subject_id>_ses-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>_behavior+ecephys+ogen.nwb`\n71\t- 28 subject directories, **174 NWB files** (one per session), 50 GB.\n72\t- Read with `pynwb.NWBHDF5IO(..., load_namespaces=True)`.\n73\t\n74\tPer file:\n75\t- `nwb.subject.subject_id` (e.g. `440956`), `nwb.subject.description` (lab ID, e.g. `SC015`), `nwb.identifier`\n76\t  (e.g. `SC015_20190208_133600_s2`).\n77\t- `nwb.trials` (`TimeIntervals`): `start_time, stop_time, trial, photostim_onset, photostim_power,\n78\t  photostim_duration, trial_uid, task, task_protocol, trial_instruction, early_lick, outcome,\n79\t  auto_water, free_water`.\n80\t  - `trial_instruction` ∈ {left, right}; `outcome` ∈ {hit, miss, ignore}; `early_lick` ∈ {early, no early};\n81\t    `task` = 'audio delay' for all 174 sessions. No missing/`N/A` values in any of these.\n82\t- `nwb.acquisition['BehavioralEvents']` — 14 `TimeSeries` with session-clock `timestamps`:\n83\t  `presample/sample/delay/go/trialend` `_start_times`/`_stop_times`, `left_lick_times`,\n84\t  `right_lick_times`, `photostim_start_times`, `photostim_stop_times` (data = laser power in mW).\n85\t- `nwb.acquisition['BehavioralTimeSeries']` — DeepLabCut side-view markers, each `(n_frames, 3)` =\n86\t  `(x, y, likelihood)` with per-frame `timestamps`: `Camera0_side_TongueTracking`,\n87\t  `Camera0_side_JawTracking`, `Camera0_side_NoseTracking` (present in **all 174** sessions),\n88\t  plus occasionally whisker / lick-port / a second camera. Frame period 3.4 ms (300 Hz).\n89\t- `nwb.units`: 39 columns incl. 15 QC metrics, `classification` ∈ {good, unlabelled},\n90\t  `anno_name` (CCF annotation; non-empty for *every* good unit and empty for every unlabelled unit),\n91\t  `spike_times`, `obs_intervals`, `is_good_trials`, `electrodes`, `electrode_group`.\n92\t- `nwb.electrodes`: `x, y, z` = CCF coordinates in µm (x = ML, midline 5700; y = DV; z = AP, bregma 5400)\n93\t  — verified against `location` JSON (`ap_location`, `ml_location`) and against the reference code's\n94\t  `global_offset_vec = (5700, 0, 5400)`.\n95\t- `nwb.electrode_groups[*].location` JSON gives the *targeted* region, e.g. `\"left ALM\"`.\n96\t\n97\t### Dataset Size (from data files)\n98\t| Statistic | Value |\n99\t|-----------|-------|\n100\t| NWB files / sessions | 174 (173 with ≥1 good unit) |\n101\t| Probe insertions (electrode groups) | 659 |\n102\t| Units (all KS2 clusters) | 272,227 |\n103\t| Good units (`classification=='good'`) | **69,453** (25.5 % of clusters) |\n104\t| Good units / session | mean 399.2, median 390, range 0–923 |\n105\t| Subjects | 28 |\n106\t| Sessions / subject | mean 6.2, range 1–11 |\n107\t| Trials (total, trials table) | 94,990 |\n108\t| Trials / session | mean 545.9, median 534, range 264–800 |\n109\t| Trials with ephys coverage | 93,930 (9 sessions have ephys for only a prefix of the behavioural trials) |\n110\t| Photostim trials | 18,588 (168/174 sessions), always 5.5 mW, always 0.5 s |\n111\t| Auto-water or free-water trials | 3,766 (4.0 %) |\n112\t| Video frame rate | 300 Hz (3.4 ms) |\n113\t\n114\tImportant structural facts discovered (all verified over all 174 files):\n115\t1. **Spike times exist only inside `[trial.start_time, trial.stop_time]`** — 0.0 % of spikes fall between\n116\t   trials. The NWB export is per-trial-windowed, not continuous.\n117\t2. `units.obs_intervals` for every unit equals the trials table's `(start_time, stop_time)` rows\n118\t   (172/174 exactly; in the other 2 it is the same length but with a small numeric difference) and\n119\t   `units.is_good_trials` has that same length. In **9 sessions** this length is *smaller* than the number\n120\t   of behavioural trials → ephys stops part-way through the session. Trials beyond that point have no\n121\t   neural data at all and must be dropped.\n122\t3. Trial windows relative to the Go cue: `go − start` ≥ 2.11 s (min over the whole dataset, median 3.15 s)\n123\t   and `stop − go` ≥ 0.155 s. **`stop − go` depends strongly on outcome**: ≈1.7–2.0 s for *hit*, 1.80 s for\n124\t   *ignore*, but only ≈0.6–0.9 s for *miss* (error) trials, which are terminated by the time-out.\n125\t   Consequence: in the requested window the last ~0.7 s of a *miss* trial contains **no recorded spikes and\n126\t   no video frames**. See Step 5 decision D6.\n127\t4. In 2 sessions (`SC045_20201216_120333_s24`, `SC053_20210220_124834_s15`) each trial's video frames are\n128\t   stored **twice**, so the marker `timestamps` are not monotonically increasing. Must sort before\n129\t   `searchsorted`.\n130\t5. 2 sessions have truncated video: `SC066_20210413_112028_s6` (video for only the first 7 of 550 trials)\n131\t   and `SC065_20210505_170309_s6` (412 of 660 trials).\n132\t6. `units.is_good_trials` is all-True except in 4 sessions (see Step 5, D5).\n133\t\n134\t---\n135\t\n136\t## Step 3: Reference Text Reading\n137\t**Status**: COMPLETE\n138\t\n139\t### Expected Statistics (from papers/methods)\n140\t| Statistic | Value | Source Quote |\n141\t|-----------|-------|--------------|\n142\t| Subjects | 28 | \"This study is based on data from 28 mice\" (datapaper) |\n143\t| Sessions | 173 behavioural sessions | \"aggregated over 660 penetrations, 173 behavioral sessions, and 28 mice\" (Fig 1J) |\n144\t| Penetrations | 660 | same |\n145\t| Good units (total) | 69,943 (25.9 % of KS2 clusters) | \"the dataset consisted of 69,943 good units recorded across 173 behavioral sessions\" (methods.txt) |\n146\t| Good units / session | median 393 | \"simultaneous measurements from hundreds of neurons (median = 393)\" |\n147\t| Good units, ALM | 8,717 | \"This method yielded 8717 good units from ALM, 7664 from striatum, 12808 from thalamus, 7495 from midbrain and 2928 from medulla, etc.\" |\n148\t| Good units, striatum | 7,664 | same |\n149\t| Good units, thalamus | 12,808 | same |\n150\t| Good units, midbrain | 7,495 | same |\n151\t| Good units, medulla | 2,928 | same |\n152\t| Trials / session | mean 476, range 130–785 | \"Mice performed on average 476 (Mean; The reference spike data are already\n165\t  Go-cue-relative; markers are aligned by subtracting `task_cue_time[0]` (= `go_start_times`).\n166\t- **Temporal binning**: sliding histogram → firing rate = spikes / bin width.\n167\t- **Trial structure**: presample → sample (0.65 s instruction tone train) → delay (1.2 s) → Go cue\n168\t  (6 kHz, 0.1 s) → 1.5 s answer period → 1.5 s consumption → trial end. Licking during sample/delay\n169\t  *replays* the sample+delay epochs, so a trial can contain several sample/delay onsets; the effective\n170\t  instruction-tone onset is the **last** sample onset before the Go cue (verified: median Go − last sample\n171\t  onset = 1.85 s = 0.65 + 1.2 s exactly).\n172\t\n173\t### Curation Steps\n174\t**Neuron curation rules** (papers + reference code):\n175\t1. Kilosort2 clusters → 15 quality metrics → five region-specific logistic-regression classifiers →\n176\t   keep only units labelled **'good'** (`units.classification == 'good'` in NWB).\n177\t2. Only units that also have a CCF annotation are used (in NWB every good unit has one).\n178\t3. (method-paper, analysis-specific) mean firing rate ≥ 2 Hz for the video→firing-rate regressions.\n179\t\n180\t**Trial curation rules** (method paper, \"Trial selection and cross-validation\"):\n181\t> \"The dataset contains trials with photoinhibition, water administration regardless of the animals'\n182\t> choice (free water trials), early licks and trials where the animal ignores the lick-spouts. These were\n183\t> excluded from all analyses.\"\n184\t\n185\tand `get_regular_trial_mask` = no early lick, no auto water, no free water, `correctness != -1`\n186\t(i.e. no *ignore*), no photostimulation.\n187\t\n188\t### Decoders Trained (reported accuracies in the papers)\n189\t| Decoded variable | Method | Accuracy |\n190\t|---|---|---|\n191\t| Choice, from **video** during sample epoch | logistic regression on embedding | ROC-AUC 0.66 ± 0.12 s.d. (n = 106 sessions); at chance in the *first half* of the sample epoch |\n192\t| Choice, from **video** during response epoch | same | ROC-AUC ≈ 0.9 (\"easily decodable from video of directional licking\") |\n193\t| Choice, single neuron, delay epoch | logistic regression on spike rate | AUC threshold 0.65 used to call a neuron \"choice modulated\" |\n194\t| Choice, population (medulla subregions) | PCA(16) + logistic regression | AUC per time point, Fig. 7 |\n195\tNote: the papers never train a *neural-population → choice/outcome/early-lick/tongue* decoder of the kind\n196\trequired here, so there is no directly comparable published accuracy number. The closest reference points\n197\tare: choice is nearly perfectly decodable from ALM/brain-wide population activity after the Go cue, and\n198\taround 0.9 AUC from video in the response epoch.\n199\t\n200\t---\n201\t\n202\t## Step 4: Check for Consistency\n203\t**Status**: COMPLETE\n204\t\n205\tMapping of reference-code (`.mat`) variables → NWB fields, and consistency checks:\n206\t\n207\t| Reference `.mat` variable | NWB equivalent | Verified |\n208\t|---|---|---|\n209\t| `task_cue_time[0,:]` (go cue) | `BehavioralEvents/go_start_times.timestamps` | 174/174 sessions: exactly one Go cue per trial, always inside `[start_time, stop_time]` |\n210\t| `task_sample_time` | `sample_start_times` / `sample_stop_times` | last sample onset → Go = 1.85 s median = 0.65 + 1.2 s ✓ |\n211\t| `task_delay_time` | `delay_start_times` | last delay onset → Go = 1.2 s median ✓ |\n212\t| `behavior_report` (1/0/−1) | `trials.outcome` (hit/miss/ignore) | choice reconstructed from `outcome`+`trial_instruction` agrees with the choice reconstructed independently from `left_lick_times`/`right_lick_times` on **99.7 %** of all 95k trials |\n213\t| `task_trial_type` ('l'/'r') | `trials.trial_instruction` | ✓ |\n214\t| `behavior_early_report` | `trials.early_lick` | ✓ |\n215\t| `behavior_is_auto_water` / `is_free_water` | `trials.auto_water` / `free_water` | ✓ |\n216\t| `task_stimulation` (power, type, on, off) | `trials.photostim_*` + `photostim_start/stop_times` | exactly one photostim event per photostim trial, 5.5 mW, 0.5 s, onset at −1.2 s or −0.5 s rel. Constant over the 80 bins |\n257\t| `trials.outcome` | `output[1]` `outcome` | 0=ignore, 1=miss, 2=hit. Constant over the 80 bins |\n258\t| `trials.early_lick` | `output[2]` `early_lick` | 0='no early', 1='early'. Constant over the 80 bins |\n259\t| `Camera0_side_TongueTracking` cols (y, likelihood) | `output[3]` `tongue_y` | per bin: frames with likelihood > 0.9 → mean y; no visible frame → class 3. Visible bins discretised by the session's 40th/60th percentiles of those binned y values → 0/1/2 |\n260\t| `units.anno_name` + `electrodes.x/y/z` | `brain_region_idx[s]` | CCF annotation → 14 coarse areas (`cache/region_map.py` rules); frontal motor cortex additionally required to be AP > 1.75 mm and |ML| < 2.0 mm to be called ALM |\n261\t| `nwb.subject.description` | `subjects` / `subject_idx` | lab mouse ID, e.g. `SC015` |\n262\t\n263\tResulting shapes: `T = 80` bins of 50 ms, `dinput = 2`, `doutput = 4`.\n264\t\n265\t`output_values`:\n266\t- `choice`: `['left', 'right', 'no lick']`\n267\t- `outcome`: `['ignore', 'miss', 'hit']`\n268\t- `early_lick`: `['no', 'yes']`\n269\t- `tongue_y`: `['<40th pct', '40-60th pct', '>60th pct', 'not visible']`\n270\t\n271\t### Key Decisions\n272\t1. **D1 — Neuron curation: `classification == 'good'` only.** This is exactly the classifier-based QC\n273\t   described in `methods.txt` / the QC white paper and used by the reference pipeline (which loads only\n274\t   the `goodunits/*.mat` index). Reproduces 69,453 units (25.5 % of clusters) vs. the paper's 69,943 (25.9 %),\n275\t   and per-area counts within 2 % (Medulla exact).\n276\t2. **D2 — Session curation: keep all sessions that have ≥1 good unit (173).** The DANDI release *is* the\n277\t   curated dataset of the paper (173 behavioural sessions), so the paper's session-selection criteria have\n278\t   already been applied upstream; re-applying my own reconstruction of them would only remove sessions the\n279\t   authors kept. The one file with 0 good units is dropped because it carries no decodable neural data.\n280\t3. **D3 — Trial curation.** Keep a trial iff\n281\t   (a) it is within the range of trials for which the probes were recording\n282\t       (`is_good_trials`/`obs_intervals` length — drops 1,060 trials in 9 sessions that have *no* ephys at all), and\n283\t   (b) it is not an auto-water and not a free-water trial (3,766 trials, 4.0 %) — following the reference\n284\t       (\"water administration regardless of the animals' choice (free water trials) … were excluded from all analyses\");\n285\t       on these trials reward is decoupled from the animal's action so the choice/outcome labels are not\n286\t       behaviourally meaningful.\n287\t   **Photostimulation, early-lick and ignore trials are deliberately kept**, even though the reference\n288\t   excludes them, because the decoder task defines photostimulation as an input and early-lick and\n289\t   `ignore` as output classes. This is an explicitly allowed discrepancy.\n290\t4. **D4 — No firing-rate threshold on neurons.** The method paper's 2 Hz cut is specific to its\n291\t   video→firing-rate ridge regressions (\"the results were not sensitive to the exact value of this\n292\t   threshold\"); it is not part of the dataset's quality control. Removing low-rate neurons would throw away\n293\t   information a population decoder can use, and the decoder's own PCA front-end handles scale. Kept all\n294\t   good units.\n295\t5. **D5 — `is_good_trials` used only to define the ephys-covered trial range**, not to drop individual\n296\t   unit×trial pairs. Only 4 sessions contain any False entries, the reference pipeline has no equivalent\n297\t   filter at all, and dropping per-unit-per-trial data is impossible in a (n_neurons, T) matrix; dropping\n298\t   the affected trials would cost 56 % of one session's trials for no principled gain.\n299\t6. **D6 — Truncated trial windows are binned as they are (zeros after the trial ends).** The NWB export\n300\t   only contains spikes/video inside `[trial.start_time, trial.stop_time]`, and *miss* trials end ≈0.8 s\n301\t   after the Go cue. 81.5 % of trials fully cover [−2.5, +1.5] s; 96.8 % cover the pre-Go part and 84.3 %\n302\t   the post-Go part. Excluding partially-covered trials would delete ~91 % of all *miss* trials and make\n303\t   the `outcome` output undecodable, so all trials are kept and the missing tail is simply empty\n304\t   (zero firing rate, tongue \"not visible\"). This is documented as a known property of the release.\n305\t7. **D7 — \"Time from tone onset\" = time since the *instruction* tone (sample epoch onset)**, not the Go\n306\t   cue: the trials are already aligned to the Go cue, so a Go-relative clock would carry no per-trial\n307\t   information, whereas the sample-onset-to-Go interval varies from 0.95 s to 10.4 s (early-lick replays)\n308\t   and is genuine task context. The *last* sample onset before the Go cue is used, because an early lick\n309\t   replays the sample+delay epochs and it is the final presentation that instructs the animal.\n310\t8. **D8 — Tongue visibility threshold: DLC likelihood > 0.9.** The likelihood distribution is strongly\n311\t   bimodal (85.6 % < 0.01, 14.0 % > 0.99), so the result is insensitive to the threshold between 0.1 and 0.99.\n312\t   A bin counts as visible if *any* frame in the 50 ms bin is above threshold (tongue protrusions last\n313\t   only ~50–100 ms), and the reported y is the mean over those frames.\n314\t   The method paper's own outlier handling (\"when the tongue was occluded … we set the tongue position to\n315\t   its mean value\") is not applicable here because the task specifies an explicit \"not visible\" class.\n316\t9. **D9 — Percentiles for the tongue discretisation are computed per session over all *visible* binned\n317\t   y values of that session** (all kept trials × 80 bins), matching \"40th percentile of y-position over\n318\t   the session\".\n319\t10. **D10 — Firing rates (Hz), not spike counts**, matching `sliding_histogram(..., rate=True)`.\n320\t11. **D11 — Brain regions**: 14 coarse areas derived from the per-unit CCF annotation, matching the region\n321\t    list used by the reference preprocessing code\n322\t    (`['ALM','Medulla','Midbrain','Striatum','Thalamus','Pons','Cerebellum','Hypothalamus','Hippocampus',\n323\t    'Orbital','OtherCortex','Olfactory','CorticalSubplate','Pallidum']`). Visible bins discretised by the session's 40th/60th percentiles of those binned y values → 0/1/2 |\n| `units.anno_name` + `electrodes.x/y/z` | `brain_region_idx[s]` | CCF annotation → 14 coarse areas (`cache/region_map.py` rules); frontal motor cortex additionally required to be AP > 1.75 mm and |ML| < 2.0 mm to be called ALM |\n| `nwb.subject.description` | `subjects` / `subject_idx` | lab mouse ID, e.g. `SC015` |\n\nResulting shapes: `T = 80` bins of 50 ms, `dinput = 2`, `doutput = 4`.\n\n`output_values`:\n- `choice`: `['left', 'right', 'no lick']`\n- `outcome`: `['ignore', 'miss', 'hit']`\n- `early_lick`: `['no', 'yes']`\n- `tongue_y`: `['<40th pct', '40-60th pct', '>60th pct', 'not visible']`\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **D1 — Neuron curation: `classification == 'good'` only.** This is exactly the classifier-based QC\n   described in `methods.txt` / the QC white paper and used by the reference pipeline (which loads only\n   the `goodunits/*.mat` index). Reproduces 69,453 units (25.5 % of clusters) vs. the paper's 69,943 (25.9 %),\n   and per-area counts within 2 % (Medulla exact).\n2. **D2 — Session curation: keep all sessions that have ≥1 good unit (173).** The DANDI release *is* the\n   curated dataset of the paper (173 behavioural sessions), so the paper's session-selection criteria have\n   already been applied upstream; re-applying my own reconstruction of them would only remove sessions the\n   authors kept. The one file with 0 good units is dropped because it carries no decodable neural data.\n3. **D3 — Trial curation.** Keep a trial iff\n   (a) it is within the range of trials for which the probes were recording\n       (`is_good_trials`/`obs_intervals` length — drops 1,060 trials in 9 sessions that have *no* ephys at all), and\n   (b) it is not an auto-water and not a free-water trial (3,766 trials, 4.0 %) — following the reference\n       (\"water administration regardless of the animals' choice (free water trials) … were excluded from all analyses\");\n       on these trials reward is decoupled from the animal's action so the choice/outcome labels are not\n       behaviourally meaningful.\n   **Photostimulation, early-lick and ignore trials are deliberately kept**, even though the reference\n   excludes them, because the decoder task defines photostimulation as an input and early-lick and\n   `ignore` as output classes. This is an explicitly allowed discrepancy.\n4. **D4 — No firing-rate threshold on neurons.** The method paper's 2 Hz cut is specific to its\n   video→firing-rate ridge regressions (\"the results were not sensitive to the exact value of this\n   threshold\"); it is not part of the dataset's quality control. Removing low-rate neurons would throw away\n   information a population decoder can use, and the decoder's own PCA front-end handles scale. Kept all\n   good units.\n5. **D5 — `is_good_trials` used only to define the ephys-covered trial range**, not to drop individual\n   unit×trial pairs. Only 4 sessions contain any False entries, the reference pipeline has no equivalent\n   filter at all, and dropping per-unit-per-trial data is impossible in a (n_neurons, T) matrix; dropping\n   the affected trials would cost 56 % of one session's trials for no principled gain.\n6. **D6 — Truncated trial windows are binned as they are (zeros after the trial ends).** The NWB export\n   only contains spikes/video inside `[trial.start_time, trial.stop_time]`, and *miss* trials end ≈0.8 s\n   after the Go cue. 81.5 % of trials fully cover [−2.5, +1.5] s; 96.8 % cover the pre-Go part and 84.3 %\n   the post-Go part. Excluding partially-covered trials would delete ~91 % of all *miss* trials and make\n   the `outcome` output undecodable, so all trials are kept and the missing tail is simply empty\n   (zero firing rate, tongue \"not visible\"). This is documented as a known property of the release.\n7. **D7 — \"Time from tone onset\" = time since the *instruction* tone (sample epoch onset)**, not the Go\n   cue: the trials are already aligned to the Go cue, so a Go-relative clock would carry no per-trial\n   information, whereas the sample-onset-to-Go interval varies from 0.95 s to 10.4 s (early-lick replays)\n   and is genuine task context. The *last* sample onset before the Go cue is used, because an early lick\n   replays the sample+delay epochs and it is the final presentation that instructs the animal.\n8. **D8 — Tongue visibility threshold: DLC likelihood > 0.9.** The likelihood distribution is strongly\n   bimodal (85.6 % < 0.01, 14.0 % > 0.99), so the result is insensitive to the threshold between 0.1 and 0.99.\n   A bin counts as visible if *any* frame in the 50 ms bin is above threshold (tongue protrusions last\n   only ~50–100 ms), and the reported y is the mean over those frames.\n   The method paper's own outlier handling (\"when the tongue was occluded … we set the tongue position to\n   its mean value\") is not applicable here because the task specifies an explicit \"not visible\" class.\n9. **D9 — Percentiles for the tongue discretisation are computed per session over all *visible* binned\n   y values of that session** (all kept trials × 80 bins), matching \"40th percentile of y-position over\n   the session\".\n10. **D10 — Firing rates (Hz), not spike counts**, matching `sliding_histogram(..., rate=True)`.\n11. **D11 — Brain regions**: 14 coarse areas derived from the per-unit CCF annotation, matching the region\n    list used by the reference preprocessing code\n    (`['ALM','Medulla','Midbrain','Striatum','Thalamus','Pons','Cerebellum','Hypothalamus','Hippocampus',\n    'Orbital','OtherCortex','Olfactory','CorticalSubplate','Pallidum']`). Hemispheres are pooled\n    (the reference splits them via the ML = 5700 µm midline; the target format's example\n    (`ALM`, `V1`) is hemisphere-agnostic).\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [x] Total good units = 69,453; median good units/session ≈ 390–393 (paper: 393)\n- [x] Per-area good-unit counts vs. paper (ALM/striatum/thalamus/midbrain/medulla)\n- [x] Choice from `outcome`+`instruction` == choice from lick times (99.7 %)\n- [x] Go − last sample onset = 1.85 s = sample (0.65 s) + delay (1.2 s)\n- [x] Photostim: 0.5 s, 5.5 mW, onset −1.2 s or −0.5 s rel. Go, one event per stim trial\n- [x] Spot check firing rate values against raw `spike_times` re-binned independently (Step 10, Check 2 — passed, incl. against the reference `sliding_histogram`)\n- [x] Spot check tongue class against raw tracking data (Step 10, Check 2 — passed)\n- [x] Spot check photostim/tone inputs against raw event timestamps (Step 10, Check 2 — passed)\n- [x] Output distributions: hit 0.685, miss 0.167, ignore 0.148, early 0.116 (Step 9 — match the raw data exactly)\n- [x] Decoder accuracy above chance on every output (Step 11 — 1.5x to 2.6x chance)\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py`. What variables in the raw data is the `neural` data derived from?\n\ni. `units['spike_times']` (the ragged spike-time column, in session-absolute seconds) restricted to the rows with `units['classification'] == 'good'`, together with `BehavioralEvents/go_start_times.timestamps`, which supply the per-trial alignment time. `units['anno_name']` plus the CCF coordinates `x,y,z` from `nwb.electrodes` (via `units['electrodes']`) supply `brain_region_idx` for those same neurons.\n\nii.\n```python\nclassification = np.asarray(units['classification'][:])\ngood = np.where(classification == 'good')[0]\n...\ngo_all = np.asarray(be['go_start_times'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\n...\nspike_lists = []\nfor i in good:\n    st = np.asarray(units['spike_times'][int(i)], dtype=np.float64)\n    if st.size > 1 and not np.all(np.diff(st) >= 0):\n        st = np.sort(st)\n    spike_lists.append(st)\n```\n\n```python\nanno = np.asarray(units['anno_name'][:])[good]\nelec_rows = np.asarray(units['electrodes'].target.data[:])[good]\netab = nwb.electrodes.to_dataframe()\nxyz = etab[['x', 'y', 'z']].values[elec_rows]\nregion_idx = assign_brain_regions(anno, xyz)\n```\n\niii. Step 1 notes this is \"Electrophysiology, not imaging → no dF/F\", and that the reference pipeline's neural representation is spike times binned into firing rates. Step 4 maps \"`neuron_single_units` (spike times rel. Go) | `units.spike_times` (session clock) − Go time\". `spike_times` is the only neural representation in the file.\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. Spike times are converted to per-bin **firing rates in Hz**. For each good unit, the 81 bin edges of every trial are concatenated into one flat absolute-time query array, a single `np.searchsorted` gives the running spike count at each edge, `np.diff` over the bin axis gives the spike count per bin, and the whole array is divided by the 50 ms bin width. Output is `float32`, shape `(n_neurons, n_trials, 80)`, then sliced into one `(n_neurons, 80)` array per trial. No smoothing, normalisation, baseline subtraction or firing-rate threshold is applied.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef bin_spike_rates(spike_times_list, go_times):\n    \"\"\"\n    Equivalent to VideoAnalysisUtils.preprocessing_DJ_2022Aug.sliding_histogram with\n    bin_width == stride == BIN_SIZE and rate=True, i.e. non-overlapping 50 ms bins\n    covering [-T_PRE, +T_POST] relative to each trial's Go cue.\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(go_times)\n    edges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()   # (n_trials*81,)\n    out = np.empty((len(spike_times_list), n_trials, N_BINS), dtype=np.float32)\n    for i, st in enumerate(spike_times_list):\n        idx = np.searchsorted(st, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n        out[i] = np.diff(idx, axis=1)\n    out /= np.float32(BIN_SIZE)\n    return out\n```\n\n```python\nneural_trials = [np.ascontiguousarray(rates[:, t, :]) for t in range(n_trials)]\n```\n\niii. Decision D10: \"**Firing rates (Hz), not spike counts**, matching `sliding_histogram(..., rate=True)`.\" Decision D4 justifies applying no rate threshold: \"The method paper's 2 Hz cut is specific to its video→firing-rate ridge regressions ('the results were not sensitive to the exact value of this threshold'); it is not part of the dataset's quality control. Removing low-rate neurons would throw away information a population decoder can use.\" Step 10 Check 2 ran the **verbatim** reference `sliding_histogram` from `preprocessing_DJ_2022Aug.py` with `bin_width = stride = 0.05` on 5 neurons × 3 trials in 4 sessions and confirmed the stored rates are numerically identical and the bin centres match.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Only units with `units['classification'] == 'good'` are retained — the verdict of the region-specific logistic-regression QC classifier. No thresholds are applied to any of the 15 individual quality metrics, and no firing-rate threshold is applied. A session with zero such units is dropped entirely. Result: 69,453 of 272,227 clusters (25.5 %), mean 401.5 and median 390 per session.\n\nii.\n```python\nclassification = np.asarray(units['classification'][:])\ngood = np.where(classification == 'good')[0]\nif len(good) == 0:\n    return {'session_id': session_id, 'skipped': 'no good units'}\n```\n\n```python\n'neuron_curation': 'units.classification == \"good\" (region-specific logistic-regression QC '\n                   'classifier of Chen, Liu et al. 2023).',\n```\n\niii. Decision D1: \"**Neuron curation: `classification == 'good'` only.** This is exactly the classifier-based QC described in `methods.txt` / the QC white paper and used by the reference pipeline (which loads only the `goodunits/*.mat` index). Reproduces 69,453 units (25.5 % of clusters) vs. the paper's 69,943 (25.9 %), and per-area counts within 2 % (Medulla exact).\" Step 4 cross-checks per-area counts against the data paper: Medulla 2,928 vs 2,928 (exact), Midbrain −0.2 %, Striatum +1.0 %, Thalamus +1.6 %, ALM +1.9 %. Step 10 Check 4 investigated the −0.7 % total shortfall and concluded the published DANDI release simply contains 490 fewer classifier-'good' units than the paper quotes, confirmed by an independent scan of all 174 files.\n\n## 2-d. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. Everything in the NWB file shares one session-absolute clock, so alignment requires no resampling or offset correction: the fixed grid of bin edges relative to the go cue is added to each trial's go-cue time to give that trial's absolute edge times, and spikes are binned directly against those edges. The alignment event is `BehavioralEvents/go_start_times.timestamps`, one per trial.\n\nii.\n```python\nT_PRE = 2.5          # s before the Go cue\nT_POST = 1.5         # s after the Go cue\nBIN_SIZE = 0.05      # s, non-overlapping bins\nN_BINS = int(round((T_PRE + T_POST) / BIN_SIZE))          # 80\nBIN_EDGES_REL = -T_PRE + np.arange(N_BINS + 1) * BIN_SIZE  # (81,) relative to Go\nBIN_CENTERS_REL = BIN_EDGES_REL[:-1] + BIN_SIZE / 2.0      # (80,)\n```\n\n```python\ngo = go_all[trial_idx]\n...\nedges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()   # (n_trials*81,)\nidx = np.searchsorted(st, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n```\n\n```python\n'temporal_alignment_event': 'Go cue onset (auditory, 6 kHz, 0.1 s), BehavioralEvents/go_start_times',\n'off_start': -T_PRE,\n'off_end': T_POST,\n```\n\niii. Step 3: \"**Temporal alignment**: everything is aligned to the **Go cue**. The reference spike data are already Go-cue-relative; markers are aligned by subtracting `task_cue_time[0]` (= `go_start_times`).\" Step 10 Check 3 records alignment as \"same\" between reference and conversion. The half-open `[lo, hi)` edge convention was explicitly checked against the reference `sliding_histogram` (Step 10, Check 5: \"half-open `[lo, hi)`, matching the reference `sliding_histogram`; verified numerically\"). The AI further validated alignment behaviourally in Step 12: population choice AUC in ALM is at chance (0.528) before the instruction tone and first rises 0.18 s after tone onset, which a one-bin misalignment would destroy.\n\n## 2-e. What is the temporal resolution (time bin size) of the converted data? Is any temporal rebinning applied?\n\ni. 80 non-overlapping 50 ms bins spanning −2.5 s to +1.5 s relative to the go cue, identical for every trial of every session (`T = 80` everywhere, confirmed by the verification log). The grid is defined once at module level as 81 relative edges and reused; spikes are binned straight from raw spike times onto that grid (no intermediate binning and hence no rebinning). The tongue video (~300 Hz) is *down*-binned onto the same 50 ms grid by averaging frames within each bin; the two scalar inputs are evaluated at the 50 ms bin centres. `metadata['time_bin_size'] = 50.0` ms.\n\nii.\n```python\nBIN_SIZE = 0.05      # s, non-overlapping bins\nN_BINS = int(round((T_PRE + T_POST) / BIN_SIZE))          # 80\nBIN_EDGES_REL = -T_PRE + np.arange(N_BINS + 1) * BIN_SIZE  # (81,) relative to Go\nBIN_CENTERS_REL = BIN_EDGES_REL[:-1] + BIN_SIZE / 2.0      # (80,)\n```\n\n```python\n'time_bin_size': BIN_SIZE * 1000.0,          # ms\n'n_time_bins': N_BINS,\n'bin_centers_s': BIN_CENTERS_REL.tolist(),\n```\n\niii. Step 4 lists this as a required, documented discrepancy from the reference: \"Bin width | 40 ms width / 3.4 ms stride (reference) | **Required discrepancy**: the task specifies 50 ms bins. We use non-overlapping 50 ms bins (width = stride = 50 ms), i.e. the same `sliding_histogram` formula with `bw = stride = 0.05`\", and likewise \"Window | [−3, +3] s (reference) | **Required discrepancy**: the task specifies [−2.5, +1.5] s.\" A constant 80 bins per trial is also what the target format requires.\n\n## 3-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Time from tone onset in seconds* derived from?\n\ni. `BehavioralEvents/sample_start_times.timestamps` (the onsets of the instruction-tone/sample epoch) together with the trial's go cue. Because an early lick replays the sample+delay epochs, a trial can contain several sample onsets; the AI takes the **last** sample onset at or before that trial's go cue.\n\nii.\n```python\nsample_t = np.asarray(be['sample_start_times'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\nsample_t = np.sort(sample_t)\n# last sample-epoch onset at or before the Go cue (an early lick replays the\n# sample+delay epochs; the final presentation is the instructive one)\nsi = np.searchsorted(sample_t, go, side='right') - 1\ntone_onset = np.where(si >= 0, sample_t[np.clip(si, 0, len(sample_t) - 1)], np.nan)\n```\n\niii. Decision D7: \"'Time from tone onset' = time since the *instruction* tone (sample epoch onset), not the Go cue: the trials are already aligned to the Go cue, so a Go-relative clock would carry no per-trial information, whereas the sample-onset-to-Go interval varies from 0.95 s to 10.4 s (early-lick replays) and is genuine task context. The *last* sample onset before the Go cue is used, because an early lick replays the sample+delay epochs and it is the final presentation that instructs the animal.\" Verified in Step 3/4: \"median Go − last sample onset = 1.85 s = 0.65 + 1.2 s exactly\", i.e. sample epoch plus delay epoch.\n\n## 3-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Time from tone onset in seconds*?\n\ni. The per-trial scalar `go − tone_onset` is added to the fixed vector of go-cue-relative bin centres, giving a (n_trials, 80) `float32` array of seconds since tone onset — a linearly increasing ramp within each trial whose offset varies per trial. A defensive fallback replaces the value with `go − median(go − tone)` if no sample onset precedes the go cue or if the found onset precedes the trial's own start time (this never triggered: \"trials w/o tone onset before Go: 0\"). Stored as row 0 of each trial's input array; observed range over the full dataset is [−1.5, 11.9] s.\n\nii.\n```python\nbad_tone = ~np.isfinite(tone_onset) | (tone_onset < start_all[trial_idx])\nif np.any(bad_tone):\n    # fall back to the median Go-to-tone interval of this session\n    fallback = np.nanmedian(go[~bad_tone] - tone_onset[~bad_tone]) if np.any(~bad_tone) else 1.85\n    tone_onset[bad_tone] = go[bad_tone] - fallback\ngo_minus_tone = go - tone_onset                                   # (n_trials,)\ntime_from_tone = (BIN_CENTERS_REL[None, :] + go_minus_tone[:, None]).astype(np.float32)\n```\n\n```python\ninput_trials = [np.stack([time_from_tone[t], photostim[t]]).astype(np.float32)\n                for t in range(n_trials)]\n```\n\niii. The instructions ask for \"Time from **tone onset** in seconds (continuous, time-varying)\", so a continuous per-bin value is emitted rather than a binary onset marker. Step 5's mapping table states the transform: \"bin-centre time minus (Go − tone-onset), in seconds; time-varying\". Step 10 Check 2 independently re-derived `bin_centre_abs − last_sample_onset_before_Go` for 24 random trials across 4 sessions and matched (24/24).\n\n## 3-c. How is the `input` *Time from tone onset in seconds* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. By construction: the input is evaluated at the **centres of the same bins** used for the spike histogram (`BIN_CENTERS_REL`, derived from the same `BIN_EDGES_REL` grid anchored on the same trial's go cue), so bin *k* of the input covers exactly the interval of bin *k* of the firing rates. No separate alignment or interpolation step exists.\n\nii.\n```python\nBIN_EDGES_REL = -T_PRE + np.arange(N_BINS + 1) * BIN_SIZE  # (81,) relative to Go\nBIN_CENTERS_REL = BIN_EDGES_REL[:-1] + BIN_SIZE / 2.0      # (80,)\n```\n```python\ntime_from_tone = (BIN_CENTERS_REL[None, :] + go_minus_tone[:, None]).astype(np.float32)\n```\n```python\nedges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()   # spikes use the same grid\n```\n\niii. Step 7's plot review states the check: \"the tone-onset input crosses zero exactly at the plotted tone onset\" in `processing_<session>.png`, where the same panel also shows the raw event time and the go cue. The single shared grid is what makes the alignment automatic.\n\n## 4-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Photostimulation* derived from?\n\ni. `BehavioralEvents/photostim_start_times.timestamps` and `BehavioralEvents/photostim_stop_times.timestamps` — the session-clock onset and offset of each laser event. (The trials table also carries `photostim_onset`/`photostim_duration`/`photostim_power`, which the AI used during exploration to verify the events, but the converted input is built from the event time series.) Sessions with no photostim events are handled by the `if len(ps_start)` guard.\n\nii.\n```python\nps_start = np.asarray(be['photostim_start_times'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\nps_stop = np.asarray(be['photostim_stop_times'].timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\norder = np.argsort(ps_start)\nps_start, ps_stop = ps_start[order], ps_stop[order]\n```\n\niii. Step 4's consistency table: \"`task_stimulation` (power, type, on, off) | `trials.photostim_*` + `photostim_start/stop_times` | exactly one photostim event per photostim trial, 5.5 mW, 0.5 s, onset at −1.2 s or −0.5 s rel. Go ✓ (matches 'late delay, 0.5 s, ends before Go')\". Using the event time series gives the laser on/off directly on the session clock, with no string parsing of the `'N/A'`-coded trials-table column, and matches the reference's `task_stimulation` on/off fields.\n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Photostimulation*?\n\ni. A binary (0.0/1.0) `float32` time series: a bin is 1 if its centre falls inside `[photostim_start, photostim_stop)` of some event, else 0. Implemented by `searchsorted` of the absolute bin centres into the sorted event-start array, taking the most recent event and testing the half-open interval. Trials with no stimulation are all-zero. Stored as row 1 of each trial's input array. 20.02 % of retained trials carry stimulation inside the window, against 20.04 % stim trials in the raw data.\n\nii.\n```python\nphotostim = np.zeros((n_trials, N_BINS), dtype=np.float32)\nif len(ps_start):\n    abs_centers = go[:, None] + BIN_CENTERS_REL[None, :]           # (n_trials, N_BINS)\n    k = np.searchsorted(ps_start, abs_centers, side='right') - 1\n    valid = k >= 0\n    kk = np.clip(k, 0, len(ps_start) - 1)\n    on = valid & (abs_centers >= ps_start[kk]) & (abs_centers < ps_stop[kk])\n    photostim[on] = 1.0\n```\n\n```python\n'Binary indicator that ALM photoinhibition was on during the bin (bin centre inside '\n'[photostim_start, photostim_stop)).',\n```\n\niii. The instructions specify \"Whether **photostimulation** is on at every time point (discrete, time-varying)\", so a per-bin binary series is required rather than a per-trial flag. Retaining photostim trials at all is decision D3's documented departure from the reference's `get_regular_trial_mask`, justified because \"the decoder task defines photostimulation as an input\". Step 7's plot review confirms \"the photostim step coincides with the raw event shading (-0.5 to 0 s or -1.2 to -0.7 s)\", and Step 10 Check 2 re-derived the input with an independent loop over the raw events for 24 trials (24/24 OK).\n\n## 4-c. How is the `input` *Photostimulation* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. The bin centres are converted to absolute session time by adding the trial's go cue (`abs_centers = go[:, None] + BIN_CENTERS_REL[None, :]`) and compared directly against the raw event timestamps, which live on the same clock. Because those centres are the centres of the same bins used for the firing rates, the photostim series is on the neural grid by construction.\n\nii.\n```python\nabs_centers = go[:, None] + BIN_CENTERS_REL[None, :]           # (n_trials, N_BINS)\nk = np.searchsorted(ps_start, abs_centers, side='right') - 1\non = valid & (abs_centers >= ps_start[kk]) & (abs_centers < ps_stop[kk])\n```\n\niii. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Early lick*?\n\ni. Follows the instructions' \"Early lick (no, yes, per-trial)\". Step 10 Check 5 notes that 3 sessions have no early-lick trials at all and were kept, \"a real property of those sessions\". Step 12 Check 1 addresses the comparatively modest 1.51× chance ratio for this binary output: \"the ceiling for a 2-class balanced accuracy is 1.0, i.e. only 2x chance, so 1.51x corresponds to 0.755 of a maximum of 1.0.\"\n\n## 8-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Tongue y-position* derived from?\n\ni. `nwb.acquisition['BehavioralTimeSeries']['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']` — the side-view DeepLabCut tracking, whose `data` is `(n_frames, 3)` = `(tongue_x, tongue_y, likelihood)` with matching per-frame `timestamps` at ~300 Hz. Column 1 (`y`) is the value; column 2 (`likelihood`) determines visibility. Present in all 174 sessions.\n\nii.\n```python\ntongue = nwb.acquisition['BehavioralTimeSeries']['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']\nttimes = np.asarray(tongue.timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\ntdata = np.asarray(tongue.data[:], dtype=np.float64)\nif ttimes.size > 1 and not np.all(np.diff(ttimes) >= 0):\n    # two sessions store every trial's frames twice -> timestamps not monotone\n    o = np.argsort(ttimes, kind='stable')\n    ttimes, tdata = ttimes[o], tdata[o]\nvisible = tdata[:, 2] > TONGUE_LIKELIHOOD_THRESH\n```\n\niii. Step 2: \"`nwb.acquisition['BehavioralTimeSeries']` — DeepLabCut side-view markers, each `(n_frames, 3)` = `(x, y, likelihood)` with per-frame `timestamps`: `Camera0_side_TongueTracking` … (present in **all 174** sessions) … Frame period 3.4 ms (300 Hz).\" Step 4 maps it to the reference's `tracking.camera_0_side.tongue_x/tongue_y`, adding that \"NWB additionally provides col 2 = DLC likelihood\", which the `.mat` export used by the reference does not expose.\n\n## 8-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Tongue y-position*?\n\ni. Frames with DLC `likelihood > 0.9` are marked visible; all others are discarded. Within each 50 ms bin of each trial, the mean `y` over the visible frames is computed (vectorised with a `searchsorted` on the visible-frame times plus a cumulative sum, so no Python loop over bins). A bin with no visible frame gets `count = 0` and mean NaN. The per-session 40th and 60th percentiles are then computed over **all visible binned means of that session** (all kept trials × 80 bins), and each visible bin is digitised against those two edges.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef bin_visible_mean(times, values, visible, go_times):\n    n_trials = len(go_times)\n    tv = times[visible]\n    yv = values[visible]\n    edges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()\n    idx = np.searchsorted(tv, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n    csum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(yv.astype(np.float64))])\n    counts = np.diff(idx, axis=1)\n    sums = np.diff(csum[idx], axis=1)\n    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):\n        mean = np.where(counts > 0, sums / np.maximum(counts, 1), np.nan)\n    return mean, counts\n```\n\n```python\nmean_y, vis_counts = bin_visible_mean(ttimes, tdata[:, 1], visible, go)\ntongue_class, pcts = discretise_tongue(mean_y, vis_counts)\n```\n\niii. Decision D8: \"**Tongue visibility threshold: DLC likelihood > 0.9.** The likelihood distribution is strongly bimodal (85.6 % < 0.01, 14.0 % > 0.99), so the result is insensitive to the threshold between 0.1 and 0.99. A bin counts as visible if *any* frame in the 50 ms bin is above threshold (tongue protrusions last only ~50–100 ms), and the reported y is the mean over those frames. The method paper's own outlier handling ('when the tongue was occluded … we set the tongue position to its mean value') is not applicable here because the task specifies an explicit 'not visible' class.\" Decision D9: \"Percentiles for the tongue discretisation are computed per session over all *visible* binned y values of that session (all kept trials × 80 bins), matching '40th percentile of y-position over the session'.\" Step 10 Check 3 flags the deliberate difference from the reference marker alignment: \"frames assigned to 50 ms bins, using the **mean** of the visible frames in each bin … at 50 ms a bin holds ~15 frames, so the mean is a better summary than the last sample.\"\n\n## 8-c. How is `output` *Tongue y-position* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Four classes, exactly as the instructions define: `0` if the binned mean y is below the session's 40th percentile, `1` if between the 40th and 60th percentiles inclusive, `2` if above the 60th percentile, and `3` (\"not visible\") if the bin contains no frame above the likelihood threshold. If a session has no visible bin at all, every bin is class 3 and the percentiles are NaN. The realised distribution is 0.098 / 0.049 / 0.098 / 0.755 — exactly 40 : 20 : 40 of the visible bins, as the percentile definition demands.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef discretise_tongue(mean_y, counts):\n    \"\"\"\n      0 : y  < 40th percentile of the session's visible y values\n      1 : 40th <= y <= 60th percentile\n      2 : y  > 60th percentile\n      3 : tongue not visible in this bin\n    \"\"\"\n    vis = counts > 0\n    out = np.full(mean_y.shape, 3, dtype=np.int64)\n    if not np.any(vis):\n        return out, (np.nan, np.nan)\n    p40, p60 = np.percentile(mean_y[vis], [TONGUE_PCT_LOW, TONGUE_PCT_HIGH])\n    y = mean_y[vis]\n    cls = np.where(y < p40, 0, np.where(y > p60, 2, 1))\n    out[vis] = cls\n    return out, (float(p40), float(p60))\n```\n\n```python\nOUTPUT_VALUES = [..., [\"<40th pct\", \"40-60th pct\", \">60th pct\", \"not visible\"]]\n```\n\niii. This is a direct transcription of the Decoder Task specification (\"0: < 40th percentile of y-position over the session; 1: 40th to 60th percentile; 2: > 60th percentile; 3: not visible\"), with the percentiles taken per session as specified. The AI verified the resulting class proportions against the definition (Step 7: \"The tongue distribution is exactly 40 % / 20 % / 40 % of the *visible* bins, as the percentile definition requires (0.100 : 0.050 : 0.100 = 4 : 2 : 4)\") and independently recomputed the percentiles from the raw tracking with a per-bin boolean mask in 4 sessions, agreeing to 1e-12 (Step 10, Check 2).\n\n## 8-d. How is `output` *Tongue y-position* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. The camera timestamps share the session-absolute clock with spikes and events, so the identical `BIN_EDGES_REL` grid anchored on each trial's go cue is used: the absolute bin edges are the same array used for spike binning, and frames are assigned to bins by `searchsorted` into the visible-frame timestamps. Bin *k* of the tongue output therefore covers exactly the same interval as bin *k* of the firing rates. Video timestamps are stably sorted first in the two sessions where each trial's frames are stored twice. Where the trial ends before +1.5 s (miss trials) or video is missing, the affected bins simply have no frames and become class 3.\n\nii.\n```python\nedges = (go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES_REL[None, :]).ravel()\nidx = np.searchsorted(tv, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n```\n```python\nif ttimes.size > 1 and not np.all(np.diff(ttimes) >= 0):\n    o = np.argsort(ttimes, kind='stable')\n    ttimes, tdata = ttimes[o], tdata[o]\n```\n\niii. Step 10 Check 3 records \"temporal alignment | Go cue (`task_cue_time[0]`), also for the video markers | Go cue (`go_start_times.timestamps`), also for the tongue marker | same\". Using one shared grid for both streams removes any possibility of a per-stream offset. Step 7's plot review confirms \"the binned tongue means track the raw visible y samples and the class switches to 'not visible' exactly where no visible frame exists\". The truncation consequence is documented in `metadata['known_limitations']` and decision D6.\n\n## 9. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni.
